blocks.text: Accounting for currency transactions follows AS-11 (The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates).

items: Initial Recognition: Recorded at the spot rate on the transaction date.
Reporting Date: Monetary items (cash, debtors) must be re-converted at the closing rate.
Exchange Differences: Gains/Losses arising from rate changes are recognized in the Profit & Loss (P&L) account.

blocks.text: Profit from Currency Derivatives is generally treated as 'Non-Speculative Business Income' because these are traded on recognized exchanges.

Tax Implication: Since it is 'Business Income', losses from currency derivatives CAN be set off against other business profits (unlike speculative losses which can only be set off against speculative profits).
STT is levied on the SELL side of the futures contract. It is not applicable to the Buy side.
